messages.text: Now I have a hyfix CM Mobile going bad. during the testing before deployment the PPS yellow light is not working.
I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Let me check the PPS LED behaviour on that unit before I say anything about it.
Searched the web · HyFix CM Mobile GEODNET PPS LED yellow light

I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist, so the HyFix is mine.

Quick context on that light before we call it bad: 
the orange / yellow PPS LED only blinks once per second when the antenna is actually seeing satellites, and it can take a few minutes
. No sky view, no PPS blink, even on a perfectly healthy unit. On a bench test indoors that is the normal result.

So, one thing first: during that test, where was the GNSS antenna? Indoors on the bench, or outside with a clear view of the sky?

Also tell me what the other two LEDs were doing (red solid, green solid or blinking) and roughly how long you left it powered.
and I am in discussion with hyfix .. that is my second CM 200 that went bad. the first one would never broadcast the the unit SSID

Noted, second CM Mobile and the first one never put out its setup SSID. That is a different failure mode, so I am treating them separately for now.

Since you already have a thread open with HyFix, keep it: these units carry a 12 month HyFix manufacturer warranty and they issue the ticket number.

Back to the one in front of you, I still need the two facts to tell a dead unit from a normal bench test:

1. Where was the GNSS antenna during the test, indoors or outside with clear sky?
2. What were the other two LEDs doing, red solid, and green solid or blinking, and how long was it powered?

If the red is solid and the green goes solid on your Wi-Fi, the unit itself is alive and we are only chasing the GNSS side, which is usually sky view, the antenna cable or the connector. If it never gets green and never broadcasts its own SSID like the first one, that is a different story and I will take it further.

Understood, no SSID means no way in at all.

One likely cause before we write it off: the setup AP often will not show on a phone. HyFix's own guidance is to do the setup from a laptop, not a mobile, so a phone scan that comes up empty does not prove the radio is dead.

Two checks, in order:

1. Which unit are we talking about now, the first one or the one on your bench today?
2. On the unit in front of you, look at the green LED. Slow blink means it is in AP mode and broadcasting, fast blink means it is trying to join a saved network, solid means it is already online. Tell me which one you see.

If it is a slow blink, scan again from a Windows or Mac laptop with the Wi-Fi antenna screwed on and the red cap ····. If the green is solid, the unit already has credentials saved and will not broadcast at all, which is why setup looks impossible: in that case find it on your router (name like MGW310_xxxxxx or similar) and open its IP in a browser.

If the green is dead or stuck fast blinking with the Wi-Fi antenna fitted and a 5V 3A supply, tell me and I will take it to JD with both units as one pattern.

solid red.. solid green ..no yellow... with the antenna outside looking up clear view of the sky.. checked conneects and cable.. all ok.. in fact .. I switched to another cm moble 200 and got a fast yellow solid red and solid green .. so I know the cable and antenna is good

That swap test is the decisive one, thank you. Same antenna, same cable, same sky: the other unit gets its PPS blink, this one does not. That rules out the antenna, the cable and the sky view and points at the GNSS front end inside this unit, which is the same LNA side that has been killing your WB200s.

Two things to close it out:

1. The unit is online (green solid), so open its web UI from your router's device list and tell me the satellite count it reports. Zero or near zero satellites with a good antenna confirms the receiver is dead rather than just unlocked.
2. Send me a clear photo of the serial number label on the bottom. HyFix will want it for your ticket anyway, and there is a known ESD issue on certain MobileCM serial ranges that is worth asking them about by serial.

Also tell me which of your orders this unit came on, so I log the fault against the right one.
Send those two things over and I will take it from there.
willl get back to ya on that.. watching a good college football at this time and my beer is getting cold

Priorities straight, go watch the game. Nothing here is urgent.

Whenever you get to it: the satellite count from the unit's web UI, a photo of the serial label, and which order it came on. Drop them in this chat and I will pick it up from there.

Enjoy the game, Robert.
